title: The biplane that sank a fleet

facts.text: On the night of 11 to 12 November 1940, Fairey Swordfish biplanes from the carrier HMS Illustrious attacked the Italian fleet at anchor in Taranto harbor.
The Swordfish was a slow, open cockpit biplane with fabric covered wings.
It was powered by a single Bristol Pegasus radial engine of 690 horsepower and could carry one 18 inch torpedo weighing 1,610 pounds.
Illustrious launched the strike from about 170 miles away. The first wave of 12 aircraft took off from 20:30, and a second wave of nine followed about an hour later.
Only some carried torpedoes. Others dropped flares to light up the harbor or bombs on the ships and oil tanks.
Three Italian battleships were hit by torpedoes: Conte di Cavour, Littorio, and Caio Duilio. Conte di Cavour was left with a hole 27 feet wide.
Britain lost two aircraft. Two airmen were killed and two were taken prisoner.
Admiral Andrew Cunningham wrote that Taranto should be remembered forever as showing that the Fleet Air Arm was the Navy's most devastating weapon.
Japanese naval officers studied the raid closely while they planned their own attack on a shallow harbor, Pearl Harbor.

declassified.fact: Japan sent a man to look. Lt. Cdr. Takeshi Naito, the assistant naval attache in Berlin, visited Taranto to study the raid, and in October 1941 he talked it over at length with Cdr. Mitsuo Fuchida, who would lead the air attack on Pearl Harbor.

body:
They flew open cockpit biplanes with fabric wings, at night, into a harbor full of battleships. Of 21 that went in, only two failed to come back.

11 November 1940. That night, Fairey Swordfish from the carrier HMS Illustrious, launched from about 170 miles away, attacked the Italian fleet at anchor in Taranto. Twelve went in the first wave and nine in the second.

Only some carried torpedoes. Others dropped flares to light up the harbor, or bombs on ships and oil tanks. Three battleships were hit by torpedoes, and Conte di Cavour was left with a hole 27 feet wide.

Two airmen were killed and two taken prisoner. Japanese naval officers studied the raid closely while they planned their own attack on a shallow harbor: Pearl Harbor.
